one_line: A lightweight experimental HTML/CSS/JS window UI framework that lets atoms open browser panels which auto-close when the player walks away.
player_facing_mechanics: Open a custom HTML window tied to a specific atom (machine/structure/etc.)
Interact with buttons/widgets in the window that send topic messages back to the game
Receive live data updates pushed into an already-open window (update_ui / browser:update)
Window automatically closes when the player moves out of adjacency range of the source atom
Window closes when the player clicks its close button (client verb frogui_close)
Atoms that opt into FROG_UI_IGNORE_PROXIMITY stay open regardless of distance
Only one frogUI window per source atom per client
data_only_parts: The bitflags FROG_UI_IGNORE_PROXIMITY and FROGUI_NO_TOPIC in code/__DEFINES/frog_ui.dm
The external CSS/JS asset surfshack13/frogui/ui.css that gets sent via browse_rsc
logic_parts: SSfrogui.fire() proximity-based auto-close loop over atom_ui_clients
open_ui() registering client/atom alists and injecting the source ref into the markup
on_topic() validating client ownership and proximity before dispatching to frog_ui_topic
close_ui()/atom_close_uis() list cleanup and signal teardown
update_ui() encoding and pushing data to the browser window
byond_specific: client << browse() / browse(null) and browse_rsc for the CSS asset
winset() on-close wiring and bare window name usage
port_notes: This is a bespoke browser-window UI bridge, not game content, so an SS14 port means reimplementing the intent on top of the existing Bound User Interface stack (UiSystem / SharedUserInterfaceComponent, ui keys, BoundUIState, UiMessage handlers) rather than translating this code directly. The auto-close-on-distance behaviour maps to a system that checks UI range each tick or on movement and closes the UI when the user leaves range (EntityLookupSystem / TransformSystem range check, or a component holding an ignore-proximity flag). The 'only one UI per atom per client' and multi-client-per-atom bookkeeping maps to the per-entity UI registry already in UiSystem, and update_ui becomes a state change pushed via the UI system rather than browser:update. A human must decide whether to keep the flag semantics (ignore proximity, no-topic/no-input windows), whether the raw HTML/CSS approach is worth preserving versus standard XAML BUI, and whether the single-UI-per-atom restriction is a design requirement or just a prototype limitation.
